title: Brand identity
summary: Naming, marks, type, color, and the rules that keep a brand recognizable when the work leaves the studio.
overview: Identity work at FRAME starts with the idea that has to survive a crowded feed, a product interface, and a quiet document. We build systems, not a single logo locked in a presentation. Every identity on this site is a fictional concept, invented so the thinking can be shown in full.
capabilities: Brand guidelines that a team can actually use

process.title: Signal
process.text: We define what the brand must be recognized for, and what it should refuse to become.

process.title: Territory
process.text: We explore distinct directions, then pressure-test them against packaging, product UI, and motion.

process.title: System
process.text: The chosen direction becomes type, color, layout, and language rules with examples, not slogans.

process.title: Handoff
process.text: Guidelines, assets, and a short working session so the people using the brand can extend it.

title: UI/UX design
summary: Product interfaces with a point of view: clear structure, sharp typography, and interaction that explains itself.
overview: We design digital products as editorial objects. Hierarchy does the talking. Flows are short. States are designed, including empty, loading, and error. The interface should feel inevitable once you have used it, and distinctive before you have.

process.title: Frame
process.text: We map the job of the product, the people using it, and the decisions the interface must support.

process.title: Structure
process.text: Flows and wireframes settle the sequence before visual design spends attention in the wrong place.

process.title: Surface
process.text: Typography, color, and motion give the structure a voice without hiding the task.

process.title: Spec
process.text: Components, states, and redlines go to engineering with the edge cases written down.

title: Web development
summary: Front-end engineering for sites and products that need to feel as considered as they look.
overview: We build with Next.js, typed components, and a performance budget. Animation is progressive. Pages work with a keyboard. Content is structured so it can be edited without breaking the layout. The studio site you are reading is the working example.

process.title: Foundation
process.text: We agree the stack, the content model, and the pages that must exist before decoration begins.

process.title: Build
process.text: Components land in the order the story needs them, with real content rather than placeholder blocks.

process.title: Harden
process.text: We test routes, forms, keyboard paths, reduced motion, and the production build.

process.title: Release
process.text: Deployment notes, environment variables, and a short handover for whoever operates the site.

title: Motion design
summary: Movement that explains hierarchy, change, and timing. If a transition has no job, it does not ship.
overview: Motion at FRAME is a narrative tool. Type arrives with intent. Images reveal through masks. Page changes stay short enough to respect a person who just wants the next page. Reduced-motion preferences are part of the design, not a patch at the end.

process.title: Intent
process.text: Each movement gets a reason: orientation, emphasis, feedback, or continuity.

process.title: Timing
process.text: We set duration and easing against the pace of the page, then cut anything that delays the task.

process.title: System
process.text: Repeated interactions share timing so the product feels like one instrument.

process.title: Fallback
process.text: Reduced motion gets a still composition that carries the same hierarchy.

title: Creative direction
summary: The through-line for identity, product, and campaign so the work feels authored rather than assembled.
overview: Creative direction is how FRAME decides what not to make. We set the concept, the references worth keeping, the tone of voice, and the sequence of releases. The rest of the studio builds inside that frame.

process.title: Listen
process.text: We learn the ambition, the constraint, and the audience that must feel the difference.

process.title: Position
process.text: A short creative platform names the idea, the tension, and the proof we will show.

process.title: Direct
process.text: Design, motion, and engineering reviews stay tied to that platform.

process.title: Edit
process.text: We remove the work that is competent but does not serve the idea.
